shipped.kurz: The capitulations of the Holy League (1571)
shipped.warum: The treaty itself, in a Spanish copy printed by Dumont, with a working translation: two hundred galleys, the cost in sixths, the Pope as judge of every quarrel, three generals deciding by majority, and the clause that no confederate may treat with the Turk alone.

The siege seen from inside the walls by an officer who survived it, in the English of 1572: six assaults, the surrender on terms, the killings in Mustafa's tent, the flaying of Bragadin, the author's escape. With the translator's dedication, his description of Cyprus and his Latin prayer for the League.

shipped.kurz: Contarini: the councils and the battle
shipped.warum: The first history of the war, Venice 1572, in Italian with a working translation: the Ottoman council of war as the Venetians imagined it, with Uluç Ali pressing for battle; the convicts freed on the League's benches and the Christian slaves manacled on the Ottoman ones; the six galleasses; Barbarigo pinned against the shore; Ali Pasha's galley taken; Uluç Ali breaking through Doria's gap; the dead by trade; the spoils divided by the League's shares; the galley that brought the news to Venice.

shipped.kurz: Peçevî: Cyprus, Lepanto and the new fleet
shipped.warum: The Ottoman side, in Ottoman Turkish with transliteration and a working translation. Cyprus: Ebussuud's fetva on when a peace may be broken, Nicosia, the mine at Famagusta, and the surrender and death of its captain after Mustafa Âlî, who was there, against Martinengo's version. Lepanto: a council of war in which the commander fears for his head, the flagship known by its three lanterns, Uluç Ali's escape. And the winter of anchors of silver and sails of satin.

shipped.kurz: Kâtip Çelebi: the broken fleet and Tunis
shipped.warum: The Ottoman naval history of 1656, from the first Ottoman press (1729), in Ottoman Turkish with transliteration and a working translation: the League's fleet as the Ottomans counted it, Uluç Ali's warning against the galleasses and the lanterns, the Bloody Cape, the dead by name, a moral for commanders, the new fleet and a quarrel with Peçevî over who paid, and the Ottoman side of Modon (1572) and of Venice's peace (1573). And the end of the war in 1574: La Goleta stormed and blown up, the Bastion of Tunis taken.

A veteran's fiction of his own war, in Spanish and English: the league, the day that broke the belief in Turkish invincibility at sea, capture, Navarino, Venice's peace, La Goleta. And the lost hand, 'on the grandest occasion'.
The ballad of 1911 that made the battle an English crusading legend, carried as reception, with its prejudices named.

planned.warum: A Venetian account of the congregations in Rome from July to November 1570: Granvelle, Pacheco and Zúñiga for Spain, Cardinal Morone for the Pope, the Venetian ambassador fighting clause by clause over Barbary, perpetuity and money. Italian, with a working translation of selected sessions.
planned.quelle: 'Négociations & Conclusioni della Lega contra il Turco … dell'Anno 1570', from an old manuscript copy, in J. Dumont, Corps universel diplomatique, vol. V, part 1 (1728), no. XCI, pp. 187–196; Internet Archive corpsuniverseldi05dumo.

planned.kurz: Fernando de Herrera, Relación de la guerra de Cipre (Seville, 1572)
planned.warum: The first Castilian history of the war, written within months, by the poet of Seville. Spanish, with a working translation of the battle chapters.
planned.quelle: Seville: Alonso Escribano, 1572; Biblioteca Nacional de España R/3794, digitised by the Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes.

planned.warum: A news print of the victory, published in the weeks after the battle: how the news reached the public.

planned.kurz: Richard Knolles, The Generall Historie of the Turkes (London, 1603)
planned.warum: The English history of the Ottoman state, with a full account of the Cyprus war and the battle. Early modern English; the OCR needs repair (long s, running side notes).

planned.kurz: Pius V and the feast of the victory (1572)
planned.warum: The bull that turned the anniversary of the battle into a feast of the Church, the start of Lepanto's afterlife in liturgy. Latin, with a working translation.
planned.quelle: Bullarum … Romanorum pontificum Taurinensis editio, vol. VII (Turin, 1862), on the Internet Archive; the bull is still to be located.

planned.warum: The baili's reports to the Senate, the nearest thing to an inside view of the Ottoman court in these years, including the peace of 1573. Italian, with a working translation.
planned.quelle: E. Albèri, Relazioni degli ambasciatori veneti al Senato, series III (Florence, 1840–55), on the Internet Archive.

planned.warum: A protestant king's heroic poem on a Catholic victory, and his preface explaining why he wrote it.
planned.quelle: Early English Books scan on the Internet Archive (1603).

planned.warum: Peçevî and Kâtip Çelebi are carried, from the fetva of 1570 to the fall of Tunis in 1574; the gap is narrower, not closed. Next candidates: Selânikî's chronicle, an eyewitness at the Porte, and the imperial orders of the Mühimme registers. Both without public-domain English, both to be carried in the same way: the printed Ottoman text, a transliteration and a working translation.
planned.quelle: Selânikî, Tarih (Istanbul 1281/1864); Mühimme registers in modern facsimile editions (copyright to be checked).
